newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees spate of firmer business.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees spate of firmer business.

text.p: Fixtures were the order of the day on the sugar freight market on Thursday but little new business emerged, shipbrokers said. CSR fixed two of its earlier bulk sugar orders from Queensland. Its order for 17,000 tonnes to Japan for 5/15 January was fixed at $19.00 while its order for Inchon for 3/15 January achieved a rate of $15.25, they said.
Cargill was said to have fixed 14,000 tonnes in bulk from Veracruz to Morocco with options of Black Sea, east Mediterranean and Baltic for December dates. Details of the rate have yet to emerge.

Genoc was on subjects with its 14,000-tonne cargo from Cuba to Mediterranean/Black Sea for end-December and Louis Dreyfus was still open with its recent bagged inquiry for 12,000 tonnes from Thailand to Colombo. Czarnikow Rionda provided the only new quoted business and was in the market for 20/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for end-January dates.
